egress.terms: Free. Downloads are proxied by ddrive, which pulls refreshed signed URLs from Discord on demand. On the read path the only cost is your own egress.

record.tooling: github.com/forscht/ddrive, 533 stars, MIT, Node 16+ / Docker, REST API with OpenAPI 3.1 spec, Postgres for metadata, web UI. Companion: `tris203/disftp` (FTP front-end for Disbox).
record.chaining: 1 Discord account x N webhook/channel pairs. Webhooks are used because 'Webhooks are not bound to a user's global rate limit' (Discord docs), so throughput scales with channel count rather than with the 50 req/s token budget.

record.limits_note: 24 MB chunk size; ~5 messages/5 s per channel even via webhook (~30 msg/min per webhook reported); metadata lives in Postgres. Lose the DB and 3 TB of chunks become unreachable in a channel (author notes a 3 TB cold start takes 30+ min).
record.reliability_note: Viable and battle-tested at multi-TB scale, but every download depends on re-deriving a 24 h signed URL, so the front-end must be alive. Two major rewrites (v2 -> v4) invalidated old layouts.

evidence.proved: 'Tested with storing 4000 GB of data on single discord channel (With max file size of 16GB)'

the project's own note, quoted: 'Now uses webhooks instead of bot/user tokens to bypass the discord rate limit', which is to say it routes around the per-token limit by using webhooks; 'I was able to upload file with 5GB of size in just 85 seconds'
'Webhooks are not bound to a user's global rate limit.'
